_comments: ORDER CONFIRMED -> SEND THE CUSTOMER THEIR DOCUMENT.
The one binding in the doc's table whose Action already exists. 'Send Document' renders the
confirmed order as its customer-facing bill, resolves the billing contacts the order itself
names, and refuses anything that is not a bill. The other four suggestions have no Action to
point at yet, and a binding whose ActionID resolves to nothing is worse than an absent one:
it looks configured.
WHY AfterUpdate AND NOT Before/Validate. Sending a bill is a side effect with an outside-world
consequence, and After* is fire-and-forget. It is explicitly NOT part of the all-or-none
transaction ConfirmOrder guarantees, which is correct in both directions: a mail relay being
down must never roll back a booked order, and a booked order must never be un-booked because a
PDF failed to render.
TRANSITION FILTER ATTACHED (`MJ_BizApps_Orders: Order Status Changed To Confirmed`).
An order is saved many times AFTER it is confirmed — posting stamps JournalEntryID, fulfilment
moves FulfillmentStatus, payments move Balance. The attached EntityActionFilter runs
`DidFieldChangeToValue(change, 'Status', 'Confirmed')` so the AfterUpdate binding fires only on
the transition into Confirmed and never on subsequent updates.
SHIPPED PENDING BY DEFAULT. Whether a company mails invoices automatically on confirmation is an
operator decision (companies using an external AR rail such as Bill.com send through the rail
instead). To enable for a deployment, scope as needed and set Status=Active on the binding and
its AfterUpdate invocation.
RE-ENTRANCY IS ALREADY HANDLED. 'Send Document' writes delivery rows, and after-hooks are guarded
against an action's own write-back re-triggering it (EntitySaveOptions.OriginatingEntityActionIDs).
'Send Document' takes OrderID as its one required input. Entity Field, not Entity Object:
the action wants the id, and passing the live BaseEntity would serialize to {} — its fields
are getters — so the action would receive an empty payload with no error anywhere.
